jobs.title: Policy Analyst, Health and Education
jobs.description:
Position:
Policy Analyst, Health and Education

Location:
New York City preferred; remote within the CSG East region considered.

The position is headquartered in CSG East's New York City office. Candidates residing elsewhere within the CSG East region may be considered for a remote work arrangement, subject to organizational needs and travel requirements.

The Council of State Governments (CSG) is the nation's only nonpartisan association of state officials serving all three branches of state government in all 50 states and the U.S. territories. CSG is a region-based forum that fosters the exchange of insights and ideas to help state officials shape public policy.

CSG East, based in New York City, supports officials and staff from its 18 member jurisdictions, which include states from Maryland to Maine, Puerto Rico, the U.S. Virgin Islands, and five Eastern Canadian provinces. To learn more about careers at CSG, and about our comprehensive benefit offerings, including medical, dental, vision, retirement, paid time off, PSLF eligibility and more, please visit our website here.

Job Summary

The Policy Analyst, Health and Education, is responsible for helping connect and inform CSG East members on health and education policy issues so that shared regional knowledge drives meaningful public impact. The Policy Analyst fulfills this objective by fostering active peer-to-peer communities via CSG East's Health and Education policy committees and developing robust policy programming that reflects the interests and issues facing CSG East's members. The Policy Analyst is expected to build strong relationships with CSG East members and partners, and helps position the organization as a trusted, nonpartisan resource for ideas, research, peer learning, and policy innovation among public officials throughout the Eastern region. The ideal Policy Analyst is an effective communicator and collaborator that equally enjoys diving deep into policy details and building relationships that help connect dots and translate good ideas into collective impact. The Policy Analyst is self-driven, exercising independent judgment under the direction of a CSG Senior Manager or Director.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Policy Committees – Staffs CSG East policy committees, working with committee chair(s) and appointed members to develop and implement committee objectives and priorities. Maintains year-round opportunities for members to learn and connect through a combination of virtual and in-person activities.
Annual Meeting – With guidance from their CSG East policy committees, develops sessions and programming at CSG East's flagship Annual Meeting and Regional Policy Forum each year. Arranges for speakers, logistical planning, and preparation of information needed for assigned sessions and programming.
Capitol Visits – Participates in CSG East visits to state capitols to engage with state officials and staff on relevant policy issues, discuss ways to participate in regional learning and discussion via CSG East, and to identify, orient, and retain appointed members to their policy committees.
Policy Forums – With support from CSG East leadership and events staff, leads the development of stand-alone policy forums of varying formats (webinars, in person summits, peer-to-peer calls, etc.) that engage members and subject matter experts on topics of interest from their committees.
Member Engagement – Develops strong relationships with legislators, legislative staff, executive branch officials, and other public sector leaders across the region, identifying opportunities for engagement and supporting member recruitment, onboarding, retention, and leadership within their assigned policy committees.
Partnerships – Builds relationships with philanthropy, academia, industry leaders, peer associations, and other subject matter experts to exchange learning, pursue collaborations, and explore possible sponsorships and grant opportunities that enrich the work of their policy committees.
Publications – Contributes to the CSG East newsletter and drafts written reports, blogs, and other media to elevate the work of CSG East, its committees, and its members.
Research – Conducts policy research and environmental scanning related to assigned issue areas; responds to member requests with concise written analyses, briefs, and resource materials; and facilitates connections with policymakers, practitioners, and subject matter experts who can provide additional insight.
Events – Attends conferences, meetings, and other events relevant to assigned policy areas. May present research and represent CSG East at partner events.
Travel – Must be willing to travel overnight for varying lengths to fulfill duties and responsibilities as needed.
Perform other assigned responsibilities and duties to support the overall mission of the organization.

Skills And Abilities

Demonstrated ability to quickly learn and synthesize complex policy issues. Expertise in every aspect of health and education policy is not expected; successful candidates will bring relevant experience and a willingness to develop new subject-matter knowledge over time.
Ability to work and conduct activities in a nonpartisan political environment.
Ability to maintain confidentiality and handle politically sensitive work.
Steadfast commitment to providing CSG members with timely, effective customer service.
Strong research skills.
Strong writing skills, including policy description and analysis as well as more general writing such as correspondence, memos and articles.
Demonstrated proficiency in oral communications.
Ability to facilitate complex policy conversation.
Analytical, with an ability to think critically, distill and present complex information in a concise manner.
Skill and competence to work effectively with a myriad of state officials, including high level executive, legislative and judicial officials.
Ability to work with leading experts in the state government field including researchers, policy experts, and program providers.
Strong interpersonal skills including self-awareness, sensitivity and valuing others.
Dedication to public service with an unfailing commitment to act with civility, be nonpartisan in performing CSG duties, and be a responsible steward of member and donor funds.
Ability to support proposal and grant writing.
Ability to work independently and to handle a variety of tasks and assignments concurrently while adhering to specific instructions, technical direction and deadlines.
Ability to work effectively in a highly collaborative team environment.
Self-motivated with ability to take initiative and see complex tasks through to completion.
Proficiency with technology used in office settings; ability to learn new software programs and evaluation/analysis techniques.
Flexibility and willingness to take on new tasks as necessary to meet evolving needs and objectives of organization and its members.
Hard working, dependable, resourceful and willing to work non-traditional hours, usually dependent on events.
Aptitude for managing projects.
Willingness to travel as needed.

Education And Experience

One (1) year of relevant work experience in state, local or federal government, a public policy organization, membership association, non-profit, or other relevant organization.
Experience working in health and/or education policy strongly preferred.
Bachelor's Degree in a relevant field of study or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
Working knowledge of the legislative, executive and judicial process.
Demonstrated experience and knowledge of general state government public policy, policy issues and programming.
Experience working collaboratively with multiple partners, with a preference for having worked with public officials.

Compensation

The salary range for this position, based in New York, NY, is $70,050 to $86,150. This salary range is subject to change based on work location and market conditions.

APPLICATION INSTRUCTIONS

Interested applicants must complete the online application and include resume and cover letter.

Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment. Equal Employment Opportunity employer (veterans/individuals with disabilities).

We are a highly collaborative team of builders and operators who invent new ways of working in an industry that historically has resisted innovation. Join us!

The Patient Services Operations team is at the center of Blink's mission to deliver exceptional patient experiences at scale. As Director of Operations Analytics & Workforce Strategy, you will turn data into decisions: determining how many people we need, how they’re deployed, and how we measure and improve performance across our contact center and pharmacy operations, including outsourced partners.
We’re looking for a sharp, analytical leader who can cut through complexity. Lead strategic analyses that turn ambiguous questions (staffing tradeoffs, site selection, build vs. buy) into clear, actionable recommendations.
Model the headcount and budget implications of operational decisions, including scenario and sensitivity analysis.
Synthesize complex analysis and recommendations/tradeoffs for executive-level stakeholders –  simplifying the numbers and logic to drive decision-making. 

Workforce Management & Real-Time Operations

Build and lead Blink’s command center capability: real-time monitoring, intraday decision-making, and cross-functional coordination to respond quickly to demand swings.
Set planning standards and performance expectations with outsourced partners.

Operational Performance & Insights

Define core metrics and KPIs, and build dashboards and reporting that give leadership visibility and understanding of performance.
Monitor key metrics (SLA, utilization, attrition, patient satisfaction) to surface trends and proactively drive deep-dive analyses to understand root causes/drivers.
Identify bottlenecks and root causes, quantify the impact of improvements, and collaborate with Operations to drive the changes that deliver them.

Leadership & Collaboration

Partner with Operations, Product & Engineering, Data, Finance, and HR to align plans, budgets, and tools.
Partner with Product & Engineering to develop capabilities that automate and scale and workforce management and reporting processes.

Qualifications

10+ years of experience in analytics, operations strategy, consulting, business operations, or workforce management, with 4+ years leading teams (ideally including managers). Bachelor’s degree in Business, Operations, Engineering, Mathematics, or a related field.
Experience in a high-volume operational environment (contact center, healthcare, logistics, or similar), with enough familiarity with capacity planning, forecasting, or staffing concepts to lead the function and learn the rest quickly.
Exceptional analytical and structured problem-solving skills, with a track record of turning complex data into decisions and measurable operational improvement.
Strong proficiency in SQL and at least one BI tool (Tableau, Looker, Power BI, or similar).
Proven ability to build financial and operational models in Excel or Python/R, including scenario and sensitivity analysis.
Experience building, leading, and developing high-performing teams and organizational capabilities in fast-paced environments.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to translate complex analyses into clear recommendations and influence stakeholders at all levels of the organization.
Thrives in dynamic, high-growth environments, effectively navigating ambiguity while maintaining focus on results; motivated by Blink's mission and improving patient outcomes through operational excellence.

It is rare to have a company that both deeply impacts its customers and is able to provide its services across a massive population.  At Blink, we have a huge impact on people when they are most vulnerable: at the intersection of their healthcare and finances. At Semperis, our mission is to be a Force for Good. Starting with being a great place to work.
We believe that when people feel valued, supported, and empowered, they do their best work. That’s why we focus on creating an employee experience rooted in purpose, growth, and balance. Semperis has been recognized as one of America’s Fastest-Growing Cybersecurity Companies by the Inc. 5000, a DUNS 100 Top Startup to Work For, and a multi-year Inc. Best Workplace awardee.

About The Role

We protect some of the world's largest, most complex hybrid identity environments, and that mission depends on earning and keeping our customers' trust. Our GRC team runs the certification and audit programs that let security-conscious enterprises, regulated industries, and government customers adopt our cloud products with confidence.

As our Cybersecurity GRC Analyst, you'll support the team across governance, risk, compliance, and customer trust work, and you'll own our annual security awareness training campaign. This is a hands-on, learning-focused role: you'll start with well-defined tasks and take on more complex work as you learn our programs.

We are a small team, so you'll get exposure to every part of GRC. In your first year, you'll gather audit evidence for SOC 2 and ISO 27001, answer customer security questionnaires, coordinate policy updates, and support our vendor risk and FedRAMP work. Experienced teammates review your work and are there to help when something is new or complex. You'll also have AI and GRC tooling, including Vanta, to help you work efficiently.

You'll succeed by being organized, responsive, and easy to work with, making it simpler for control owners to provide what audits and customers need.

+++No sponsorship will be provided for this role. Candidate must be eligible to work in the country in which you apply+++

What You Will Do

Security Awareness Training

Follow up on overdue security training, then lead the annual Security and Compliance Training campaign: work with People Operations and Legal on the curriculum, set up enrollments in the training platform, track completion weekly, and escalate overdue training.
Handle training exceptions, keep training records ready as audit evidence, and gather feedback to improve next year's campaign.

Customer Trust

Answer customer security questionnaires, starting with simpler requests and taking on more within your first few months. Escalate complex requests to senior teammates.
Check answers for accuracy, confirm requestors are under NDA before sharing information, and help maintain our answer library and Trust Center content.

Audit and Compliance Support

Learn our FedRAMP program and support the FedRAMP ISSO as needed.
Gather and organize evidence for SOC 2 and ISO 27001 audits, confirm it meets each request, and prepare it for review before it goes to auditors.

Governance and Risk Support

Coordinate security policy updates: route policies for review and approval, publish approved versions, and keep version history and change records.
Recommend improvements to team processes, status reporting, and work priorities.
Support vendor risk work by tracking annual recertification of critical vendors and sending information requests to vendors.
Provide administrative support for the cyber risk register, including intake of new risk information.
Use our GRC platform (Vanta) and help find ways to automate manual tasks and evidence collection.

What You Will Bring (Required)

One of the following: a CISA, CRISC, or CISSP certification, or a degree in Cybersecurity.
At least 6 months of experience in a GRC role.
Strong organization, attention to detail, and follow-through on deadlines.
Clear written and verbal communication skills.
Working knowledge of Microsoft 365 and Excel, and comfort using AI-assisted tools.

Preferred Qualifications

2 to 3 years of work experience in IT, cybersecurity, or GRC.
Exposure to SOC 2, ISO 27001, or FedRAMP audits, in a supporting role or as an auditee.
Experience with a modern GRC platform such as Vanta.
Experience answering customer security questionnaires.
Experience at a SaaS, cloud, or cybersecurity company.

Success Measures (First Year)

Assignments are completed correctly and on time, with good judgment about when to ask for help.
Overdue training is followed up and the annual training campaign is delivered on schedule.
You share ownership of customer security questionnaires within your first few months.
Audit evidence for SOC 2 and ISO 27001 is complete and on time.

Why Join Us

You'll learn GRC across every domain alongside experienced GRC, security, and engineering professionals at a fast-growing cybersecurity company. As your skills grow, you can take on more complex customer trust, policy, risk, and FedRAMP work.

Why Join Semperis?

You’ll be part of a global team on the front lines of cybersecurity innovation. At Semperis, we celebrate curiosity, integrity, and people who take initiative. If you’re someone who sees the glass as half full, embraces challenges as growth opportunities, and values a healthy balance between work and life—we’d love to meet you.
